note:
Second attempt at the review section. The first used multi-column — a three-across grid of image + quote + text link — which was NOT what Malcolm meant. Tatcha's construction, captured and examined properly: ONE review at a time, one large square model image on the left, a white product card floating ON TOP of that image carrying a thumbnail, the product name and its price, and the star rating, reviewer name and quote set large to the right.

The theme has an exact native equivalent: `shop-the-look`. It takes the large image, positions real product blocks over it by horizontal/vertical percentage, and styles the floating card via product_card_background / product_card_text_color. Because the block references a real Shopify product, the card pulls the live name and price automatically — the same behaviour as Tatcha's 'The Dewy Skin Cream / From $25'. No hand-built markup, which is what Malcolm asked for.

One review is built first so the layout can be confirmed before repeating it. shop-the-look renders one image per section, so a Tatcha-style rotation would mean either stacked sections or a custom carousel — a decision to take after seeing this.

Product is referenced by GID; if the card fails to render, the fallback is the bare handle.

First push exposed two faults: the product setting takes the HANDLE, not a GID (the GID rendered Shopify's placeholder backpack, 'Product' and a default price), and `title` did not render at all, so the rating and reviewer name are folded into the rich text instead.
